### Mendoza Vineyards for Architecture Lovers

A team of two architects together make up the firm Bormida y Yanzon.

If you love architecture and design, you’d be well-served to take their projects into account when planning your wine tasting itinerary.

Together they have designed the most impressive buildings that dot the landscape across Mendoza.

They incorporate innovative materials such as concrete, stone, wood, and glass into their projects that result in a building that echoes the land around it.

Their winery projects are both modern and functional but also fit perfectly into the natural landscape of Mendoza.

A few noteworthy bodegas that they’ve designed include Salentien, O. Fournier, Septima (above) and DiamAndes.

If you’re interested in learning more, put [this article](https://wideprint.com.ar/profesionales/contemporaneos/bormida-yanzon-arquitectos/) about them through Google Translate.

For a complete list of their projects visit their [website](http://www.bormidayanzon.com/), click on *proyectos*, then *bodegas*.

![]()*Mendoza in Winter*

![]()*Mendoza in Spring*

[…]

## Sample Mendoza Winery Itineraries

Here are two sample itineraries for my two favorite Mendoza wine regions: Lujan de Cuyo & The Uco Valley.

They’re tried and tested (they’re our itineraries from our more recent trip!).

Take them and copy them identically or use them as a guide, substituting your own favorite wineries that are nearby.

Whichever you choose, I hope you have an excellent day of wine tasting!

### Uco Valley Itinerary

If I were to plan a wine tasting in Valle de Uco Itinerary for a friend, this is the day I’d schedule for them.

1. [Alfa Crux](https://www.agostinowinegroup.com/alfa-crux-wines) – 10 am – This winery is the furthest, so start here and work your way back up. Their first tour is at 10 am, so wake up early and eat a hearty breakfast to prepare yourself for all that wine you’ll be drinking today.
2. [SuperUco](https://superuco.com/) – 12 pm – It will take you 40 minutes to drive here from Alfa Crux so you’ll need to schedule SuperUco for no earlier than noon.
3. Optional Bonus Tasting at [Corazon del Sol](https://www.corazondelsol.com/) or [ Solo Contigo](http://solocontigowine.com/): If you have time for an extra tasting after SuperUco and before your lunch reservation, see if you can squeeze in a quick tasting at one of these two wineries. They’re on the same property as SuperUco (as they form part of The Vines).
4. [Bodega Azul](https://bodegalaazul.com/) – 2:30 pm for lunch – You’ll spend the remaining hours of your afternoon hours here, so sit back and enjoy the meal. Stretch your legs in between courses under the Mendoza sun looking at the mountains, or lounge on the sofas in the grass after lunch.

![A bottle of wine on a table next to a basket of bread]()*Wine and lunch at Ojo de Agua in Lujan de Cuyo*

### Lujan de Cuyo Itinerary

This is my ideal day in Lujan de Cuyo, and it’s tried and tested because this is how we spent a day here this year.

You’ll need a car or a driver for this itinerary as these wineries aren’t reachable by bikes rented from Baccus. It’s worth the effort, I promise.

1. [A16](http://a16sa.com/en/) – 10 am – Start your day with a tasting and a tour at A16.
2. There are a LOT of wineries in this area, pick from: Ruca Malen, Cruzat, Vinas Cobos, Septima, Susan Balbo for winery #2 at 11:30
3. [Ojo de Agua](https://ojodeagua.ch/) – 1:30 pm for a winery lunch – It took us about 15-20 minutes to drive to Ojo de Agua from Melipal (which has since been bought out by another corporation). Enjoy a leisurely lunch, we finished lunch at 4 pm.
4. Optional Bonus Tasting after lunch. Wineries close at 5 or 6 so if you play your cards right you can squeeze in one last tasting (no tour) after Ojo de Agua. Choose from: Septima, Cruzat, Viña Cobos or Ruca Malen.

# Wine Tour By Bus

[5 reviews](#reviews)

Are you interested in experiencing the **Wine Route**? 🍷  
We have an exceptional option just for you.

The **Wine Bus** offers a modern way to **discover and enjoy Mendoza’s Wine Routes**, featuring guaranteed departures and no minimum number of passengers required. It’s perfect for anyone wishing to **dive deep into wine culture** and tour wineries open to visitors, with **guided tours, wine tastings, sales, and top-notch culinary experiences**.

This service operates with a **Hop On Hop Off** system, giving you the flexibility to **get on and off the bus throughout the day**. You’re free to select the wineries you want to visit and choose your preferred tour type: Full Day: 10 hours of immersive vineyard experiences.

- 🕔 **Half Day:** 5 hours

This service features over 25 fixed stops, allowing you to board from Mendoza City, Guaymallén, Maipú, Luján de Cuyo, Tupungato, or Tunuyán—always near your accommodation. The bus guarantees reserved seats for every route, so you can enjoy winery visits and tastings without any hassle. At each winery, select and pay directly for the experiences you prefer. It’s the most convenient, safe, and enjoyable way to explore the wineries of Valle de Uco without worrying about transportation.

## Tour Description

## **TOURS:**

[…]

### 🌞 Wine Route “El Sol” – Tuesday

**Wineries and venues visited:**  
 Casa El Enemigo Vigil • Bressia • Viña Las Perdices • Séptima • Tierras Altas • Cruzat

**Full Day Transfer Ticket:** Access up to three wineries and enjoy a lunch at one during your visit: Casa Vigil + Bressia or Viña las Perdices + lunch (choose from Terrazas de los Andes or Séptima) + Tierras Altas or Cruzat.

- Lunch at Tierras Altas includes participation in the Malbec Experience at Tierras Altas.
- Lunch at Séptima includes a visit and tasting at Bodega Cruzat.

**Half Day Transfer Ticket Morning:** Visit **two wineries**: Casa El Enemigo Vigil and your choice of Bressia or Viña Las Perdices.

**Half Day Transfer Ticket Afternoon:** Visit **two wineries**: Séptima and Cruzat.

  

### 🍷 “Luján Sur” Wine Route – Friday

**Wineries and destinations visited:**  
 Chandon • Zolo • Budeguer • Casarena • Terrazas de Los Andes

**Full Day Transfer Ticket:** Visit up to **three wineries and enjoy lunch at one** on this route: Chandon + Zolo or Budeguer + lunch, visit, and tasting at your choice of Terrazas de los Andes or Casarena.

**Half Day Transfer Ticket Morning:** Visit **two wineries**: Chandon + Zolo or Budeguer.

**Half Day Transfer Ticket Afternoon:** Visit **two wineries**: Chandon and Casarena.

  

### 🏔 “Valle de Uco” Wine Trail – Sundays

**  
Andeluna Winery • GAIA Restaurant (at Domaine Bousquet Winery) • Salentein Inn • Salentein Winery**

****Full Day Transfer Ticket:** This route is available exclusively as a **Full Day** tour, including visits to Andeluna, a lunch (choose between GAIA Restaurant or Salentein Inn), and Salentein Winery.**

[…]

### What exactly does the Wine Tour by Bus include and what is the itinerary like?

The wine tour by bus typically includes tourist bus transportation with a driver, a wine tourism expert, visits to selected wineries, vineyard tours, and guided tastings of local wines such as Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, or blends. The itinerary usually combines an explanation of the winemaking process, a tour of the cellars, and time for photos and shopping in the wine shop. Some tours may offer wine pairings or snacks, and in some cases, lunch is optional. Entrance fees and tastings are usually included; personal expenses and tips are not. The winery route and schedules may vary depending on the season and availability. Check the operator's website in the "Includes" section for the most up-to-date details.

[…]

### Are there age requirements, accessibility requirements, and in what language is the guided tour conducted?

To participate in wine tastings in Argentina, the minimum legal age is 18; minors may accompany the family tour, but may not consume alcohol. Regarding accessibility, the tour bus and some wineries may have stairs, uneven surfaces, or confined spaces; if you require assistance or have reduced mobility, please inform us when booking so we can assess options and availability. The tour is usually offered with a Spanish-speaking guide and frequently in English; please confirm the language available on your chosen date. If there are wine pairings, please inform us of any allergies or special dietary requirements in advance. It is recommended to avoid driving after the tasting and to follow the guidelines for responsible consumption during the wine tourism experience.
